gap.missing_evidence: An independently inspectable numerical duration for the isolated ED environmental-services bed-space cleaning interval, with audit sample size/denominator and observations, and evidence separating active cleaning work from embedded process delay, remains unavailable. The captured primary XML defines the process and Figure 2 caption but does not contain Figure 2 image values.
gap.owner: P1/P4 ED resource and process-evidence coordinator
gap.impact: The article's 48-minute mean is the full elapsed bed-turnaround process between successive patients occupying a bed, comprising notification, cleaning, and clean-bed idle. It is not the isolated cleaning component or active EVS labor time. The indexed 9-minute Figure 2 component was not verified against figure pixels and must not be promoted. The 4-minute Zhu clinician procedure-preparation/clean-up task is a different activity. No cleaning duration, empirical distribution, or generic/Cairns default is supported by this evidence packet.
searches_performed: Inspected Chartier et al., Improving Emergency Department flow through optimized bed utilization, BMJ Quality Improvement Reports 5 (2016), u206156.w2532, DOI 10.1136/bmjquality.u206156.w2532; canonical full text https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5051383/ and Europe PMC version PMC5051383.1, published 2016-09-28. Captured source is .artifacts/sources/p12-support/cleaning-pmc5051383.xml, SHA-256 721f7cf7d543898a032790b322fdc1cd295da555575fba560813d18fc159c6d8; accessed 2026-10-01. Primary XML paragraph 'As a process measure...' defines turnaround from patient 1 leaving until patient 2 arriving, and separates notification, EVS cleaning (sheet change, surface sanitizing, refuse removal, WhiteBoard set to clean), and clean-bed idle until triage assigns a new patient. Text reports only the overall 48-minute average and directs readers to Figure 2 for component times. Figure 2 XML caption says it breaks down component periods, but the cited pixels were not acquired/inspected; the 9-minute component remains unverified.

Acquisition notes report that volunteer on-site audit sample size, individual observations, variance/distribution, and cleaning-resource roster are not reported. The unrelated 2,354 patient visits over nine weeks are the baseline high-acuity time-to-bed cohort, not the cleaning audit denominator. No audit-level cleaning records or separate active-work observations are present in the captured materials.

Article licence recorded in the source acquisition notes: CC BY-NC 2.0; commercial reuse requires separate permission. Source is openly accessible; no figure image or underlying audit data were redistributed.

Reviewed supplied R6 report 6 lines 29-31 as report lineage only. It distinguishes 48-minute total turnaround, the unverified reported 9-minute cleaning component, 26-minute clean-bed idle, and Zhu's distinct 4-minute clinician procedure preparation/clean-up. R6 is not primary-source verification.

Targeted gap remains: obtain inspectable Figure 2 pixels or audit-level source data with n, values, site/period, and start/stop timestamps; distinguish EVS active work from notification, status-update, and clean-bed idle intervals. If unavailable, preserve unknown duration and seek local EVS bed-state/roster observations for Cairns-specific use.
gap.next_action: Obtain the Figure 2 image in a form that can be inspected or request the underlying volunteer audit records. Record audit n, population/site/period, raw or summarized component values, and timestamp rules; establish whether the cleaning interval measures active EVS work or elapsed work-plus-update time. Seek local EVS bed-state observations if a Cairns profile is required. Until verified, keep cleaning duration unresolved and do not substitute 9, 48, or 4 minutes.
